Title: Analysis of the Independent Clans - Followers of Set

Messages.Author: Todd Banister
Messages.Body:
Analysis of the Followers of Set

General Overview:
Within the World of Darkness the Followers of Set are based primarily in
Haiti and Egypt and are considered to be the ultimate manipulators,
infiltrators and deceivers with their mastery of moral and spiritual
corruption. Their abusive style carries over to the CCG exceptionally well.

Along with the Assamites, the Followers of Set arrived in the CCG world in
the Ancient Hearts expansion set. Since then they have been tempting and
corrupting minions at will and using them for the clan's own personal
objectives.

Overview of Vampires and Clan Specific cards:
Lalitha (2) ser
Khalil Anvari (3) pre ser
Hadrian Garrick (4) obf pre [+1 hand damage]
Nepata (4) obf pre ser
Dedefra (5) nec obf SER [+1 hand damage vs. Camarilla vampires]
Aisha (6) ani aus PRE ser [may burn a blood for +1 intercept]
Amisa (8) OBF pre pro SER [2 votes. May tap a vamp above 7 cap as an
action]
Kephamamos (8) dom obf pre SER [2 votes. +1 bleed]
Saqqaf (9) cel for OBF PRE SER [Gain a pool for performing a serpentis
action.]
Kemintiri (10) aus dom OBF PRE SER THA [Gets +1 bleed/+1 stealth and can
fight vs. Ventrue.]

The Followers of Set are based around the skills of obfuscate, presence and
serpentis. These skills are primarily offensive leaving very little in
defense (intercept or bounce). With the combination of obfuscate and
presence the Followers of Set can strike for quick and devastating bleeds.
This combination of skills could also be the basis for a stealthy voting
deck. The only drawback for the Followers of Set in the voting angle is that
both of their vampires that have votes only possess minor presence. The
serpentis skill is the essence of the Followers of Set and gives them a wide
range of tactics for manipulation.

Upon examining the makeup of the vampires in the clan one will notice the
lack of superior skills from the lower to mid ranged vampires. Superior
serpentis is found on half of the clan members but only on one with the
capacity lower than eight. The same is true for superior presence. Obfuscate
is even worse in that the first superior skill cannot be found until Amisa
at eight capacity. Of the eight different out-of-clan disciplines the
Followers of Set only have two with more than one each (aus and dom have
two). Both the smaller (capacity four and below) and larger (capacity eight
and above) sized vampires are excellent for the clan but the mid ranged
vampires are definitely lacking in composition.

One of the major strengths of the clan comes from their clan specific cards.
Corruption has incredible power (although only against ones prey) and alone
has created a variety of strategies due to it being a clan based instead of
a skill-based card. The Opium Den, The Path of Typhon and the Mummy's Tongue
work very well for the clan in support of their minions. The Realm of the
Black Sun is the clan's only source of pool gain (besides Saqqaf's serpentis
actions) and has a nice twist to it. The rest of the clan specific cards
fail to deliver their intended value. The Grand Temple of Set costs too much
for the ability and is too easily burned by any vampire as a directed action
due to Followers of Set having only light intercept (from Aisha). The
Kherebutu Mummy bleeds and punches nicely for an ally but uses necromancy
instead of serpentis and is just to fragile to cost a whopping five pool.

Overview of Serpentis :
The serpentis skill offers the Followers of Set a wide variety of options to
its minions. The heart of serpentis is the ability to steal allies,
retainers and vampires with stealth. In combat serpentis allow its minions
to prevent aggravated damage, steal blood and end combat if needed. The only
thing that serpentis does not offer the clan is any form of defense. The
Followers of Set have minimal defense from voters and no way of dealing with
any bleed action with more than one stealth. The Followers of Set would be
greatly assisted if serpentis would allow them to defend against they
predator in any way.

Suggestions:
Be very careful here: Do not create any small (capacity four and under)
Followers of Set vampires with presence. There is currently enough of these
vampires in the game.
· Superior in-clan disciplines: The Followers of Set desperately need to
have a few mid ranged (capacity five through seven) vampires that include
some superior in-clan disciplines. The clan would greatly benefit from a
vampire like Sir Walter Nash of the Ventrue with all three superior in-clan
disciplines. Another vampire that would help them out would be a three
capacity vampire with only superior serpentis. Of the out-of-clan
disciplines the one that the Followers of Set need more of is auspex.
· A little voting help: The stealthy voting strategy would be helped out if
the Followers of Set had one more vampire that had a vote or two. This would
also assist in their vote defense.
· Defense and options to burn Corruption counters: The Followers of Set need
to be able to place Corruption counters on their predator. It would be ideal
if they were allowed to burn these counters for a variety of options with
the effect of manipulating other minions. Some of these options could
include burning some of the counters to cancel or change a vampire's votes,
stop a minion from taking an action to bleed them for a round, or to reduce
a bleed by a pool or two (like telepathic counter). The idea of burning
Corruption counters would be consistent with the spirit of the clan and give
them a much-needed form of defense.

Main Disciplines Obf, Pre, Ser

Sum. Votes 4 Avg. Votes 0.40

Tha Vic
1/0 2/0 1/0 2/0 1/0 1/0 4/3 5/3 1/0 4/5
0/1

2 clans)
Total number of votes within the clan: 4 (16th best)
Average percent of In-Clan-Disciplines within the clan: 76.08 (15th best)

with 3 clans)

Todd Banister
V:EKN Prince of Atlanta
Scribe of the Assamites

I will agree that the card "Corruption"is underpowered, and is another
nearly wallpaper card that either needs a re-write or a complimentary
card to help it.

One strike against Vampire stealing has to do with the Golden Rule of
Card Ownership. I'm not sure what the most recent DCI rule is, but in
the NJL when a player is ousted from the game he/she takes all of
their cards with them.

Which means decks based on stealing Vampires/Minions are somewhat at
a disadvantage as the stolen goods vanish after trouncing your Prey.

As for getting rid of corruption counters, I would suggest that a
vampire could burn X blood to remove X corruption counters.
Corruption would have been better written as a unique location where
Setites could take (D) actions to place corruption counter on
Vampires. Of course, such a place would need to be burnable by a (D)
action. Fairs fair after all..

defence (or intercept) such things are just pants. Keeping it as

wanting to interfere directly and overtly.

certainly cause the location intercepts (Radio Tower and Newspapers) to

>

Rewrite Corruption: "(D) Place this card on any minion. Any Settite
may take a +1 stealth (D) action to place a Corruption counter on the
minion with this card." END of card text - note removal of built-in
steal clause. Now print cards to burn corruption counters to steal
minions for a turn, for good, etc. etc. as above. It would open up a
WORLD to them, and no longer do you need 30 Corruption cards to really
make it go. =)

>Card Ownership. I'm not sure what the most recent DCI rule is, but in

DCI is "you take all cards you control". So if your vampire or
location or stuff was nicked, it stays nicked.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:

DCI doesn't address the issue, meaning that the official rulebook rule
applies:

1.3. The Golden Rule of Card Ownership

Your cards are never transferred to another player permanently as a result
of card play. At the end of the game, the cards you began the game with are
returned to you. If you are ousted, all the cards you control are burned.
Any of your opponents' cards you may control are placed in their respective
owners' ash heaps (see Important Terms, sec. 1.1). Any of your cards that
other players control remain until the controlling players are ousted. The
only exception to this rule is the optional ante (see Playing for Ante,
sec. 2.4): ante cards may change hands permanently.

--

Messages.Author: Eugene Earnshaw-Whyte
Messages.Body:
The setites, as they stand, are pretty much incapable of effectively
defending themselves from bleed or votes, and have a fair amount of
difficulty against potence/rush, too. This pretty much forces them to go for
a quick kill strategy, using their small minions to bleed repeatedly at
stealth with social charms and such.

They can't defend well against bleed, because their disciplines give them no
resources for intercept or bounce. One could, I suppose, stack up pack
tactics, but any half-decent bleeder will laugh his way through that, unless
you include enough cards to seriously hamper you doing other things
effectively. The best defence against voting -- votes and intercept on the
board -- they are weak on. And their only defence in combat is S;CE, which
any competent rush deck will have a strategy for dealing with.

Setites are therefore forced in to a very stereotyped pattern. Since
Serpentis is virtually useless (form of corruption is worthwhile, form of
the serpent is marginal, as is tongue of the serpent), the one (very
effective) avenue open to them is stealth bleed, which they can do quite
well, given their access to Majesty and Propaganda on top of the stealth.
The poor mix of disciplines on their vampires hampers them somewhat in this
regard, but they can compensate by using low pool minions and lots of
masters.

The Setites require two things: mid pool vampires with somewhat better
disciplines, and more usefuls serpentis cards. If serpentis was a more
flexible discipline, the Setites would have more options as a clan in terms
of legitimate strategies. It would be a very nice touch if serpentis was
given some good vote-related action modifiers: this would serve to
counterbalance the Setites lack of votes on the board, making a voting
strategy more realistic. Either that, or some clan specific voting cards
(perhaps designed to reflect Setite Thaumaturgical paths, which have some
political uses...)

They can always Kindred Restructure themselves out of the way.... Justicar
Retribution is another option, as is Banishment.

They do lack permanent votes, yes. However, they can use Dread Gaze etc.

> any competent rush deck will have a strategy for dealing with.

It's not their *only* defence. Maneuvers are available via Form of the
Serpent and Obfuscate, as are dodges. Elysium and disciplineless
equipment are also available - Leather Jacket being very good combat
defence, IME.

> Setites are therefore forced in to a very stereotyped pattern. Since
> Serpentis is virtually useless (form of corruption is worthwhile, form of
> the serpent is marginal, as is tongue of the serpent),

You miss out Temptation, which is a superb card.

Corruption is also viable, if played properly.

> the one (very
> effective) avenue open to them is stealth bleed, which they can do quite
> well, given their access to Majesty and Propaganda on top of the stealth.
> The poor mix of disciplines on their vampires hampers them somewhat in this
> regard, but they can compensate by using low pool minions and lots of
> masters.

Agreed. The discipline mix they have is bad for stealth-bleed or
stealth-vote, or a mixture of the two.

Messages.Author: Eugene Earnshaw-Whyte
Messages.Body:
Ah, that's the plan.

A good player with access to lots of cards can put together very creditable
decks, regardless of whether the clan is best suited for that particular
strategy. Obfuscate is a very valuable adjunct to voting, obviously, as is
presence, so discipline-wise, Setites seem to be well positioned. A setite
voting deck can be done, and I'm sure, done pretty well. So can a Lasombra
voting deck. But both are harder to do (for opposite reasons) and, I think,
generally less effective than some of the more traditional voting styles --
ventrue small minion, Large IC/Princes with obfuscate, etc.
